title: Exact critical probabilities for a wide class of graphs
statement: Find p_c(G) for a wide class of graphs G. Kesten notes at once that a solution 'would not have any explanatory value': the critical probabilities determined so far depend heavily on special symmetry properties of the underlying graph, and their values vary from graph to graph.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for exact critical probabilities for classes of transitive graphs, plus the arXiv listings of Duminil-Copin and collaborators mined for this intake. Nothing found that computes p_c for a class wider than the self-dual planar lattices and the tree/nonamenable examples already known in 2002; recent activity (Duminil-Copin and Panis 2024-2025, and the high-dimensional survey fetched here as highdim_random_walk_2026) is about exponents, not exact p_c. Kept open. Not exhaustively searched: the isoradial-graph literature, where Grimmett and Manolescu give p_c for a wide isoradial family; that family is a genuine partial answer and is the closest known relative.

attempt.method: Ask what a nonvacuous version of the question could say, by cataloguing the only two mechanisms that have ever produced an exact p_c: (i) a self-duality that forces the critical point to a fixed point of the duality map, upgraded to an identification by a box-crossing (RSW) property; (ii) an exact recursion on a tree or a tree-like transitive graph.
attempt.result: Mechanism (i) is not a property of the graph alone but of a pair (graph, dual): it delivers p_c only when the duality map has a unique fixed point in (0,1) AND the crossing probabilities at that point are bounded away from 0 and 1. That is why the star-triangle family (square, triangular, hexagonal, and the isoradial graphs of Grimmett-Manolescu) is the natural closure of the method, and why it stops there. Mechanism (ii) gives p_c = 1/(b-1) on the b-ary tree and survives on nonamenable Cayley graphs only in the qualitative form p_c < 1, not as a formula. A version of the question with content, which the known values can already address, is: is the set {p_c(G) : G an infinite connected vertex-transitive graph} dense in (0,1)? The known values accumulate at 0 (p_c(Z^d) is asymptotically 1/(2d)) and at 1 (long-range one-dimensional chains), so density is the natural sharpening rather than a search for more closed forms. This is a reformulation of the source's question, not progress on it.
attempt.obstruction: No invariant of a transitive graph is known that predicts whether p_c is algebraic. Every existing proof of an exact value runs through an algebraic identity between the model and its dual, and no such identity exists off the star-triangle family, so one cannot even rule out that p_c of some simple non-self-dual planar lattice is transcendental. The density reformulation is not free either: it needs a family along which p_c moves continuously, and continuity of p_c is known only along the slab approximations of Grimmett-Marstrand.
attempt.key_identity: Self-duality forces p_c + p_c^* = 1 only when the crossing probabilities at the self-dual point are bounded away from 0 and 1; without a box-crossing property the fixed point of the duality map need not be critical.

title: Existence of the surface-order limit for the supercritical cluster-size distribution
statement: For site percolation on Z^d with p > p_c it is known that there are constants 0 < C_4(p), C_5(p) < infinity with C_4(p) <= -n^{-(d-1)/d} log P_p{|C(v)| = n} <= C_5(p) for all large n. Does lim_{n to infinity} n^{-(d-1)/d} log P_p{|C(v)| = n} exist?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the surface-order large deviations for supercritical percolation cluster size. Returned the Wulff-construction literature: Alexander-Chayes-Chayes (d = 2), Cerf, 'Large deviations for three dimensional supercritical percolation' (Asterisque 267, 2000), Cerf-Pisztora (2000, 2001), Bodineau (1999). These give a surface-order large deviation principle for the SHAPE of a large finite cluster with speed n^{(d-1)/d} and the Wulff functional as rate. I did not verify from the papers themselves whether they yield the limit for the LOCAL event {|C(v)| = n} rather than {|C(v)| >= n}, at every p > p_c and every d >= 3; the d >= 3 results were originally stated above the slab threshold. Kept admitted with that lead recorded: anyone merging this row should check Cerf-Pisztora before treating it as open.

attempt.method: Split the question into the half the Wulff theory delivers and the half it does not. Write W_p for the Wulff constant, the infimum of the integral of the surface tension over the boundary of a body of unit volume, so that the surface-order LDP for the monotone event reads -lim n^{-(d-1)/d} log P_p{|C(v)| >= n} = W_p.
attempt.result: The upper half is immediate: {|C(v)| = n} is contained in {|C(v)| >= n}, so limsup n^{-(d-1)/d} log P_p{|C(v)| = n} <= -W_p, given only the monotone LDP. The matching lower bound is a volume-adjustment statement: it would suffice to modify a near-Wulff cluster of volume in [n, n + n^{(d-1)/d}] into one of volume exactly n at cost exp(o(n^{(d-1)/d})). Here is the budget that decides the problem, and it is the reason the naive argument fails: adding or deleting m boundary sites costs at most exp(Cm), while the surplus volume to be shed is itself of order n^{(d-1)/d} - exactly the order of the entire exponent. The trimming argument is therefore critical, not subcritical. Stating where the two rates could differ is sharper than the source's own remark, but it is a localisation of the difficulty, not a proof that the limit exists.
attempt.obstruction: Trimming a supercritical cluster is not local: closing boundary sites to shed volume can disconnect the droplet, or merge the finite cluster with the infinite one and destroy the conditioning event {|C(v)| < infinity}. Any repair must control the volume through an event measurable with respect to Pisztora's coarse-grained block field, and that field resolves volumes only up to a multiplicative factor (1 + eps) - precisely the resolution an exact-volume question refuses.
attempt.key_identity: P_p{|C| >= n} = sum over m >= n of P_p{|C| = m} with a nondecreasing exponent in m; the two rates agree exactly when the sum is dominated by its first term, so the whole content is that the exponent is not flat to leading order over a window of length n.

title: Left continuity of the percolation function between p_c and p_u
statement: For a transitive graph G, is p -> theta_v(p) = P_p(|C(v)| = infinity) left continuous on [p_c, p_u]? Kesten notes that on Z^d, where p_c = p_u, this is equivalent to theta(p_c) = 0, known in 2002 for d = 2 and for d >= 19.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on continuity of theta at criticality for transitive graphs and on the non-uniqueness interval. Fitzner-van der Hofstad (2017) lowered the high-dimensional threshold from d >= 19 to d >= 11, and Hutchcroft has proved theta(p_c) = 0 for large classes of nonamenable transitive graphs and of transitive graphs of exponential growth. I did not find, and did not establish the absence of, a statement covering left continuity on the whole non-uniqueness interval [p_c, p_u] for a general transitive graph. Kept admitted; the Hutchcroft nonamenable results are the closest known relative.

attempt.method: Separate the two statements the question conflates: continuity in the interior of the interval, and the boundary value at p_c.
attempt.result: Right continuity is free everywhere and needs no hypothesis: theta(p) = inf_n P_p(v <-> boundary of B_n) is a decreasing limit of polynomials in p, hence upper semicontinuous, and theta is nondecreasing, so theta is right continuous on [0,1]. Left continuity on any interval where the infinite cluster is a.s. unique is the van den Berg-Keane argument. The live content of the question is therefore exactly the non-uniqueness window (p_c, p_u), where the infinite cluster has infinitely many components and the van den Berg-Keane proof, which uses uniqueness to prevent the number of infinite clusters from jumping, is simply unavailable. Saying it this way is sharper than the source's reduction, which only records the p_c = p_u case. What is NOT claimed: nothing here suggests left continuity fails on (p_c, p_u); the honest status of the interior is 'no known proof', not 'expected to fail'.
attempt.obstruction: A jump of theta at some p in (p_c, p_u) would mean a positive density of vertices joins the infinite clusters at a single parameter. Excluding it by a Russo derivative bound needs an influence estimate at p, and in the non-uniqueness phase the pivotal vertex for {v lies in an infinite cluster} need not be unique or locally identifiable, since v may join any of infinitely many infinite clusters. The mass-transport principle controls the NUMBER of infinite clusters but says nothing about theta itself.
attempt.key_identity: theta = inf_n P_p(v <-> partial B_n): an infimum of continuous increasing functions is upper semicontinuous, which gives right continuity for free and leaves only the left limit in question.

title: Power laws, universality and scaling relations for percolation
statement: Prove that the percolation critical exponents (beta, gamma, nu, delta, eta, defined through theta(p), chi(p), the correlation length and P_{p_c}{|C| >= n}) exist as genuine power laws; prove universality, that they depend only on the dimension and not on the lattice; and prove the scaling relations among them. Known in 2002 for site percolation on the triangular lattice and for d >= 19 by the lace expansion, with no progress in d = 3, 4, 5.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for percolation critical exponents in intermediate dimensions 2024-2025. The recent results are on two-point functions: Duminil-Copin and Panis 2024/2025 for the Ising and phi^4 models (sharp for d >= 5, almost sharp with a logarithmic correction at d = 4), and a 2025 revisit of one-arm exponents in high dimensions, plus a spread-out d > 6 derivation of mean-field behaviour. None establishes existence of exponents in d = 3, 4, 5, and none establishes universality in any dimension. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask which of the three demands is logically weakest, since the source poses them as one problem; order them existence, scaling relations, universality, and test whether that order is right.
attempt.result: The order is wrong in one place, and that is the useful observation: scaling relations are NOT downstream of existence. Several are proved as two-sided inequalities between limsup and liminf exponents by differential-inequality arguments (Aizenman-Barsky, Aizenman-Newman) that never assume a limit exists. So the honest decomposition is that the relations already hold in inequality form and what is missing is the coincidence of limsup and liminf. Universality is strictly harder than both and has no route that avoids an exactly solved representative of the class - which is why even the two-dimensional case, where only site percolation on the triangular lattice is solved, is not a proof of universality. A caution about what does not count as progress: if the exponents exist, Fisher's relation gamma = nu(2 - eta) follows from the definitions plus the infrared bound and carries no extra information.
attempt.obstruction: Existence of an exponent asserts that a log-log slope has a genuine limit, and percolation offers no subadditivity in p to force one. The only tool that produces exponents, the lace expansion, needs the triangle condition, a strictly high-dimensional input false in d = 3, 4, 5; the two-dimensional tools (RSW, conformal invariance) are planar. Dimensions three to five have neither, and that is the entire difficulty.
attempt.key_identity: Aizenman-Barsky and Aizenman-Newman give the mean-field bounds beta <= 1, gamma >= 1, delta >= 2 with no exponent existence assumed; existence is a separate, unaddressed statement.

title: Any power bound at all for percolation quantities in dimensions three, four and five
statement: For Bernoulli percolation on Z^d with 3 <= d <= 5, find upper and lower power bounds for theta(p), chi(p), xi(p) and P_{p_c}{|C| >= n}. Kesten notes that bounds on one side are known for most of these but that no bound of the form theta(p) <= C |p - p_c|^{C'} has been proved for 3 <= d <= 5, not even for p < p_c, and calls this 'probably the most fundamental bound to prove'.
status_search: Same search as E0004. The 2024-2025 Duminil-Copin and Panis lower bounds on two-point functions concern the Ising and phi^4 models and are sharp only for d >= 5 (almost sharp at d = 4); their percolation results are for spread-out models above six dimensions. No polynomial bound of the missing type for nearest-neighbour percolation in d = 3, 4, 5 was found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Test how much of the missing bound is already forced by the inequalities the source itself quotes, in particular Kesten's chi(p) >= C |log(p_c - p)|^{-(d-1)/d} (p_c - p)^{-1/d} for p < p_c, obtained by iterating the critical crossing estimate over k blocks.
attempt.result: That chain gives a power lower bound on chi with a poor exponent and gives nothing at all on theta, because the passage from chi to theta needs the other direction. The point that must be stated carefully: Aizenman-Barsky's inequality theta(p) >= c(p - p_c) is a LOWER bound on theta, and the mean-field bound beta <= 1 is a statement in the same direction; neither supplies the sought upper bound theta(p) <= C(p - p_c)^{C'}, and no trivial inequality does. What the reduction does give is an equivalence worth recording: an upper bound of that form is exactly a quantitative version of continuity of theta at p_c, which is the statement missing in d = 3, 4, 5.
attempt.obstruction: Every known proof of an upper bound on theta near criticality goes through the one-arm probability at p_c, via theta(p) <= P_{p_c}(0 <-> partial B_{L(p)}) with L(p) the near-critical correlation length, and then needs polynomial decay of the critical one-arm probability. That decay comes from RSW in d = 2 and from the lace expansion in high dimensions. In d = 3, 4, 5 there is no proof that P_{p_c}(0 <-> partial B_n) decays polynomially at all, and without it no power of |p - p_c| can be produced by any known relation for L(p).
attempt.key_identity: theta(p) <= P_{p_c}(0 <-> partial B_{L(p)}): the missing power bound on theta is exactly a missing polynomial critical one-arm bound together with a power relation for the near-critical correlation length.

title: The closed-path functional N(v) in critical percolation in three and more dimensions
statement: Let N(v) := inf{number of closed vertices in any path from 0 to v} in critical percolation. On Z^2 it is known that [sigma_{p_c}(N(v))]^{-1}[N(v) - E_{p_c} N(v)] satisfies a central limit theorem, with E_{p_c} N(v) of order log|v| and standard deviation of order (log|v|)^{1/2}. On Z^d with d >= 3 it is only known that N(v) = O(|v|^{eps}) a.s. for every eps > 0. Improve the bound for N(v) and find a limit theorem for N(v) in dimension >= 3.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for the minimal number of closed edges on a path in critical percolation in higher dimensions. The two-dimensional central limit theorem (Kesten-Zhang) remains the standing reference; no d >= 3 result of either kind surfaced. Not exhaustively searched: the high-dimensional chemical-distance literature (Kozma-Nachmias and successors) concerns the OPEN chemical distance, a different functional from N(v), so it does not bear on this row. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask what the two-dimensional proof actually uses and which ingredient survives in d >= 3. The Z^2 argument renormalises over dyadic annuli: at each of the log|v| scales the path must cross a critical annulus, the closed-vertex cost per annulus is tight, the costs are asymptotically independent across scales by RSW decoupling, and the CLT is a Lindeberg sum over scales.
attempt.result: Both the mean of order log|v| and the standard deviation of order (log|v|)^{1/2} come from the same structure - one asymptotically independent O(1) contribution per scale. Consequently the shape of the answer in d >= 3 is decided by a single question: is the per-scale cost still tight? If it is, the same Lindeberg argument gives E N(v) asymptotically c log|v| and a central limit theorem with variance of order log|v|, in any dimension where a cross-scale decoupling is available. This collapses the source's two demands ('improve the bound' and 'find a limit theorem') into one estimate. It is a reduction, not a bound: tightness of the per-scale cost is precisely what is unknown.
attempt.obstruction: Cross-scale decoupling in d = 2 is RSW. There is no RSW in d >= 3, and the only decoupling available for critical percolation there is the high-dimensional two-point function estimate, a statement about connection probabilities rather than about the number of closed vertices on an optimal path. Worse, in d >= 3 an optimal path has more ways to route around obstacles, so the per-scale cost is plausibly growing rather than tight, and the trivial |v|^{eps} bound does not even exclude a polynomial mean.
attempt.key_identity: N(v) is a sum over dyadic scales of per-annulus closed-vertex costs; in d = 2 both the log|v| mean and the log|v| variance follow from tightness plus asymptotic independence of those costs, so one tightness statement decides the shape of the answer in every dimension.
